fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. The men and women bring “…brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry.” (Exodus 35:22). Rings and necklaces are right there on that list. And they present that gold as a wave offering to the LORD.

Cups and bowls, friend? Nice try, but this verse is a jewelry box, not a kitchen cabinet. The people bring “…brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry.” (Exodus 35:22). I'd know a cabinet when I saw one. I lived in a drawer for years.

Crowns and shields sound mighty, but that's not what shows up here. The verse says “…brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry.” (Exodus 35:22). The men and women are bringing what they wear, from earrings to necklaces. Nobody's marching in with armor.

The text doesn't mention any tribal leaders in this scene, friend. The craftsmen stop their work and go straight to Moses with their report: “The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the LORD has commanded us to do.” (Exodus 36:5). No meeting gets called. They just walk it right over to him, and I bet they were grinning.
